item.text: {"facts":[{"source_id":"SRC-a7bc69b31d7654ce","start_unit":2,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"In October 2023, MERICS reported that Xi Jinping had reshaped China’s political economy so party and state institutions guide economic actors toward strategic goals, with technological self-reliance prioritized over consumption-led growth and some socioeconomic targets.","question_ids":["5B.1","5B.4","5B.6","8B.1","8B.2","8B.6"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Directly describes the policy direction in 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The report explicitly attributes the economic-governance shift and strategic agenda to Xi Jinping.","limitations":["Analytical assessment rather than an official budget or outcome dataset."]},{"source_id":"SRC-a7faa0b2edf8c287","start_unit":11,"end_unit":12,"fact_summary":"In September 2023, Hoover reported that Xi’s strategy harnessed private capital to restore CCP political authority while pursuing technological self-reliance, supply-chain leverage, surveillance, propaganda, and defense goals.","question_ids":["5B.1","5B.4","8B.1","8B.2","8B.3","8B.6"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Published and applicable in 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The report directly attributes the strategy to Xi Jinping.","limitations":["Policy analysis does not independently quantify implementation or outcomes."]},{"source_id":"SRC-3e200bf8241a404c","start_unit":13,"end_unit":15,"fact_summary":"On August 26, 2023, Xi affirmed the outcomes of Xinjiang policies and called for continued counterterrorism and stability measures, correct views on ethnicity, history, and religion, and a unified Chinese national consciousness.","question_ids":["3B.3","3B.5","3B.7","4B.3","4B.7","8B.1","8B.2","8B.9"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Specific dated event in 2023.","ruler_attribution":"Xi delivered the cited speech and endorsed continuation of the policies.","limitations":["The source is a human-rights organization’s assessment of the policy consequences."]},{"source_id":"SRC-3e200bf8241a404c","start_unit":15,"end_unit":16,"fact_summary":"Human Rights Watch reported in August 2023 that Xinjiang’s coercive system continued: although some reeducation camps appeared closed, there had been no mass prison release, approximately half a million Turkic Muslims had been imprisoned since the crackdown began, and family contact remained severely restricted.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.2","3B.7","3B.10","8B.6","8B.7","8B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Assessment published in 2023 of continuing conditions during the period.","ruler_attribution":"The report attributes the continuing system to Chinese government policy under Xi’s leadership.","limitations":["The estimate is attributed to HRW’s synthesis and concerns the broader crackdown beginning before 2023."]},{"source_id":"SRC-95241680d96760ef","start_unit":2,"end_unit":2,"fact_summary":"The 2023 U.S. State Department report found genocide and crimes against humanity occurred in China during 2023 against predominantly Muslim Uyghurs and other minorities, including mass arbitrary detention, torture, forced labor, coercive reproductive practices, and severe restrictions on expression, religion, movement, and political participation; it also found no credible government steps to identify or punish abusive officials.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.2","3B.4","3B.5","3B.7","3B.9","3B.10","7B.2","7B.6","7B.7"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Explicitly covers 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The findings concern the Chinese government during Xi Jinping’s rule; the excerpt does not establish a personal order by Xi for each abuse.","limitations":["Country-level assessment; individual attribution within the state apparatus is not specified for every finding."]},{"source_id":"SRC-95241680d96760ef","start_unit":4,"end_unit":5,"fact_summary":"During 2023, authorities continued arbitrary detention and disappearance practices, including residential surveillance at designated locations and liuzhi; politically sensitive detainees could be held incommunicado for months, with prolonged pretrial detention and restricted access to counsel.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.4","3B.5","3B.8","7B.6","7B.7"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The report documents practices continuing during 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The practices were carried out through state and CCP security and supervisory bodies under Xi’s government.","limitations":["The excerpt describes systemic practice rather than a single Xi-directed detention."]},{"source_id":"SRC-95241680d96760ef","start_unit":7,"end_unit":8,"fact_summary":"In 2023, authorities maintained tight control over media and online speech, punished criticism of the CCP or Xi, and continued to prosecute journalists and activists; the report cited 90 writers held in custody in 2022 and at least 102 journalists detained according to RSF data, with repression continuing into 2023.","question_ids":["3B.3","3B.8","4B.3","4B.6","4B.9","7B.1","7B.2"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Includes 2023 incidents and continuing conditions, with some supporting figures from 2022.","ruler_attribution":"The censorship and prosecutions were conducted by authorities under Xi’s CCP leadership.","limitations":["Some cited counts predate 2023 and are used as context for continuing repression."]},{"source_id":"SRC-95241680d96760ef","start_unit":8,"end_unit":10,"fact_summary":"In 2023, authorities detained or prosecuted writers, journalists, and activists for speech; Ruan Xiaohuan received seven years, Xu Zhiyong 14 years, and Chang Weiping three and a half years, while media outlets and editors faced penalties or dismissal for reporting that challenged official policy.","question_ids":["3B.8","4B.3","4B.6","4B.9","7B.1","7B.2","7B.7"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Contains dated 2023 sentences and 2023 reporting on continuing repression.","ruler_attribution":"The punishments were imposed by courts and authorities operating under Xi’s government.","limitations":["The excerpt does not show Xi personally ordered each case."]},{"source_id":"SRC-95241680d96760ef","start_unit":11,"end_unit":12,"fact_summary":"In 2023, China’s internet remained subject to extensive censorship, real-name identification, content deletion, and criminal penalties; in May the Cyberspace Administration reported deleting 1.4 million posts and permanently closing 67,000 accounts, while generative-AI rules required politically compliant content.","question_ids":["1B.9","3B.5","4B.6","4B.9","7B.1","7B.2","8B.2","8B.6"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Contains 2023 measures and enforcement figures.","ruler_attribution":"The CAC and related bodies implemented the controls within Xi’s party-state system.","limitations":["The source reports administrative actions but does not quantify Xi’s personal involvement in each enforcement action."]},{"source_id":"SRC-95241680d96760ef","start_unit":16,"end_unit":16,"fact_summary":"During 2023, the anti-corruption campaign continued through the NSC-CCDI, but the report found enforcement inconsistent and opaque and cited credible reports that investigations and liuzhi detentions were sometimes politically motivated or used to purge rivals.","question_ids":["4B.4","5B.5","7B.2","7B.6","7B.7","7B.9"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Explicitly describes the campaign and institutional practice during 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The campaign operated through institutions established and directed within Xi’s CCP leadership.","limitations":["The report distinguishes official anti-corruption activity from allegations of political use."]},{"source_id":"SRC-95241680d96760ef","start_unit":17,"end_unit":18,"fact_summary":"In 2023, domestic violence remained widespread, women earned on average 35 percent less than men doing similar work, and authorities often failed to enforce protections; the government issued voluntary workplace guidance on female labor protection and sexual harassment on March 8.","question_ids":["3B.7","6B.3","6B.8","8B.2","8B.6","8B.7"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Contains a dated 2023 policy and 2023 country findings, with some underlying indicators from earlier reporting.","ruler_attribution":"The ministries issued the guidance; the broader enforcement findings concern the Chinese government.","limitations":["The wage-gap and domestic-violence figures are not necessarily measured solely in 2023."]},{"source_id":"SRC-95241680d96760ef","start_unit":18,"end_unit":19,"fact_summary":"During 2023, coercive population-control measures continued to target Uyghur and other minority women, including forced abortions, sterilizations, involuntary IUD insertions, and pregnancy checks; the report also found assimilation policies restricting minority language, religion, movement, and employment.","question_ids":["3B.7","6B.3","6B.8","8B.6","8B.7","8B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The report documents continuation during 2023, while noting policies that began earlier.","ruler_attribution":"The practices were implemented through CCP and government policy under Xi’s leadership.","limitations":["Some cited evidence concerns multiyear programs rather than a single 2023 decision."]},{"source_id":"SRC-95241680d96760ef","start_unit":23,"end_unit":24,"fact_summary":"In 2023, independent unions remained illegal and the ACFTU remained the only recognized union; workers’ rights advocacy faced surveillance, detention, and harassment, while average enterprise workweeks were nearly 49 hours and labor-law enforcement was inconsistent.","question_ids":["5B.4","5B.5","5B.8","6B.2","6B.7","8B.6","8B.7"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Contains 2023 labor findings and 2023 administrative conditions.","ruler_attribution":"The labor framework and enforcement were maintained by the government and CCP under Xi.","limitations":["The average-hours series began before 2023 and is used to describe the continuing condition."]},{"source_id":"SRC-80443784f861c3df","start_unit":3,"end_unit":4,"fact_summary":"During the June 2022–May 2023 coverage period, China remained the world’s worst-ranked abuser of internet freedom for the ninth consecutive year, with a score of 9/100; authorities censored protests, criticism of Xi, economic reporting, and online discussion of COVID-19 consequences.","question_ids":["3B.8","4B.3","4B.6","4B.9","7B.1","7B.2","8B.6","8B.9"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Coverage period substantially overlaps 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The report links the repression to the CCP system and Xi’s consolidated leadership.","limitations":["The reporting window begins in 2022 and ends in May 2023."]},{"source_id":"SRC-80443784f861c3df","start_unit":4,"end_unit":5,"fact_summary":"After nationwide zero-COVID protests, authorities removed protest posts, expanded censorship, detained protesters, and ultimately ended the zero-COVID policy; the report also recorded 1.07 billion internet users and a 75.6 percent penetration rate by December 2022.","question_ids":["3B.8","3B.9","4B.9","6B.6","8B.8","8B.9"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The policy reversal and repression occurred at the end of 2022 and shaped the 2023 coverage period.","ruler_attribution":"The policy and response were actions of Xi’s government.","limitations":["The principal protest and policy-reversal events occurred before 2023."]},{"source_id":"SRC-80443784f861c3df","start_unit":21,"end_unit":22,"fact_summary":"In 2023, Chinese regulators required technology firms to discontinue access to ChatGPT, disclose plans for domestic AI chatbots, and subject generative-AI services to political-content controls; Chinese chatbots reportedly refused questions about Xi.","question_ids":["1B.9","3B.5","4B.6","4B.9","8B.2","8B.6"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Specific 2023 regulatory actions and observations.","ruler_attribution":"The controls were imposed by regulators within Xi’s party-state.","limitations":["The measures address information control and AI governance, not the full range of catastrophic AI risks."]},{"source_id":"SRC-80443784f861c3df","start_unit":30,"end_unit":31,"fact_summary":"In 2023, Chinese rules required platforms to review posts, filter harmful content, and ensure generative-AI outputs embodied core socialist values; the system lacked transparency and formal avenues to appeal censorship decisions.","question_ids":["1B.9","4B.6","4B.9","7B.2","8B.2","8B.6"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Includes rules effective or issued in 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The CAC and related regulators implemented the framework under Xi’s leadership.","limitations":["The source evaluates civil-liberty consequences more than technical AI safety."]},{"source_id":"SRC-80443784f861c3df","start_unit":52,"end_unit":55,"fact_summary":"During 2023, online speech led to detention and imprisonment, including a three-year sentence for Uyghur student Kamile Wayit, 14 years for Xu Zhiyong, three and a half years for Chang Weiping, and a reported arrest related to ChatGPT-generated content.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.5","3B.8","4B.3","4B.9","7B.7"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Contains dated 2023 prosecutions and a 2023 arrest.","ruler_attribution":"The detentions and sentences were imposed by state authorities and courts under Xi’s government.","limitations":["The excerpt summarizes reported cases and does not establish personal orders from Xi."]},{"source_id":"SRC-80443784f861c3df","start_unit":66,"end_unit":68,"fact_summary":"In 2023, authorities continued requiring technology companies to assist surveillance and retain user data; a March restructuring plan created a national data bureau, while a Wuxi authority claimed it deleted one billion pandemic-data records, a claim the source said could not be independently verified.","question_ids":["1B.3","1B.9","3B.5","4B.9","7B.2","8B.2","8B.8"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Contains a 2023 restructuring plan and reported 2023 data-deletion claim, alongside continuing legal rules.","ruler_attribution":"The data and surveillance framework was maintained by Xi’s government; the restructuring was a national government decision.","limitations":["The deletion claim was not independently verified."]}],"documents_with_no_material_fact":["SRC-78632289555bec7b","SRC-550dfe9bb39f4836","SRC-4488e7627af0de44","SRC-df9e71d6234b6dbf","SRC-60e9d169b635545d","SRC-0b223243f19754ed","SRC-a7faa0b2edf8c287","SRC-246b4ae78aa2c877"],"batch_limitations":["Several supplied sources were metadata pages, summaries, or excerpts rather than complete underlying reports, limiting event-level attribution.","Some evidence describes policies originating before 2023 but continuing into or affecting the 2023 period; those records identify the temporal limitation.","No supplied document provided material evidence about Xi’s nuclear doctrine, arms control, conventional war authorization, or direct personal financial enrichment during 2023."]}
